title: KCET 2010 Maths
subject: maths
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column A1

questions.q: The chord of the circle $x^2+y^2-4x=0$ which is bisected at $(1, 0)$ is perpendicular to the line
questions.explanation: The circle has centre $(2,0)$. The radius to the midpoint $(1,0)$ is horizontal, so the chord bisected there is vertical ($x=1$), which is perpendicular to $y=1$.

questions.q: In $\triangle ABC$, if $a=2$, $B=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{2}$ and $C=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{1}{3}$, then $(A, b)=$
questions.explanation: $\tan(B+C)=\dfrac{1/2+1/3}{1-1/6}=1$, so $B+C=\pi/4$, $A=3\pi/4$. Using $\sin B=1/\sqrt5$, $\sin A=\sqrt2/2$, the sine rule gives $b=a\sin B/\sin A=2\sqrt2/\sqrt5$.

questions.q: The straight line $2x+3y-k=0$, $k>0$ cuts the X- and Y-axes at $A$ and $B$. The area of $\triangle OAB$, where $O$ is the origin, is 12 sq. units. The equation of the circle having $AB$ as diameter is
questions.explanation: Intercepts are $A=(k/2,0)$, $B=(0,k/3)$; area $=k^2/12=12$ gives $k=12$, so $A=(6,0)$, $B=(0,4)$. Circle on $AB$ as diameter: $(x-6)x+(y-4)y=0$, i.e. $x^2+y^2-6x-4y=0$.

questions.q: Let $P(x, y)$ be the midpoint of the line joining $(1, 0)$ to a point on the curve $y^2=\begin{vmatrix}x+1 & x+2\\ x+3 & x+5\end{vmatrix}$. The locus of $P$ is symmetrical about
questions.explanation: The determinant equals $x-1$, so the curve is $y^2=x-1$. For midpoint $P(X,Y)$ of $(1,0)$ and $(x,y)$: $x=2X-1$, $y=2Y$, giving $4Y^2=2X-2$, i.e. $Y^2=(X-1)/2$, symmetric about the X-axis.

questions.q: The function $f(x)=|x-2|+x$ is
questions.explanation: $f(x)=2$ for $x<2$ and $f(x)=2x-2$ for $x\ge2$; both pieces agree at $x=2$ (value $2$), so $f$ is continuous everywhere, in particular at $x=0$ and $x=2$, but its derivative jumps from $0$ to $2$ at $x=2$.

questions.q: If $a$, $-a$, $b$ are the roots of $x^3-5x^2-x+5=0$, then $b$ is a root of
questions.explanation: Sum of products in pairs $=-a^2=-1\Rightarrow a^2=1$; product of roots $=-a^2b=-5\Rightarrow b=5$. Checking, $x=5$ satisfies $x^2-3x-10=0$.

questions.q: In the binomial expansion of $(1+x)^{15}$, the coefficients of $x^r$ and $x^{r+3}$ are equal. Then $r$ is
questions.explanation: $\binom{15}{r}=\binom{15}{r+3}$ requires $r+(r+3)=15$, so $r=6$.

questions.q: The $n^{th}$ term of the series $1+3+7+13+21+\ldots$ is 9901. The value of $n$ is
questions.explanation: The $n^{th}$ term is $T_n=n^2-n+1$. Setting $n^2-n+1=9901$ gives $n^2-n-9900=0$, whose positive root is $n=100$.

questions.q: If $\dfrac{1}{(3-5x)(2+3x)}=\dfrac{A}{3-5x}+\dfrac{B}{2+3x}$, then $A:B$ is
questions.explanation: Putting $x=3/5$ gives $A=5/19$; putting $x=-2/3$ gives $B=3/19$; so $A:B=5:3$.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT true?
options: $\{(p\to q)\wedge(q\to r)\}\to(p\to r)$ is a tautology.
questions.explanation: Since $p\wedge\sim q\equiv\sim(p\to q)$, the statement $(p\wedge\sim q)\leftrightarrow(p\to q)$ is $X\leftrightarrow\sim X$, which is always false, not a tautology; the other three statements are genuinely true.

questions.q: Let $R$ be an equivalence relation defined on a set containing 6 elements. The minimum number of ordered pairs that $R$ should contain is
questions.explanation: The smallest equivalence relation is the identity relation (each element related only to itself), which has exactly 6 ordered pairs.

questions.q: The line joining $A(2, -7)$ and $B(6, 5)$ is divided into 4 equal parts by the points $P, Q$ and $R$ such that $AQ=RP=QB$. The midpoint of $PR$ is
questions.explanation: $P,Q,R$ divide $AB$ into four equal parts, so $Q$ is the midpoint of $AB$ and, by symmetry, also the midpoint of $PR$: $Q=\left(\dfrac{2+6}{2},\dfrac{-7+5}{2}\right)=(4,-1)$.

questions.q: Let $P\equiv(-1, 0)$, $Q\equiv(0, 0)$ and $R\equiv(3, 3\sqrt3)$ be three points. The equation of the bisector of the angle $PQR$ is
questions.explanation: Unit vectors along $QP$ and $QR$ are $(-1,0)$ and $(1/2,\sqrt3/2)$; their sum $(-1/2,\sqrt3/2)$ gives the bisector direction, with slope $-\sqrt3$, i.e. $\sqrt3x+y=0$.

questions.q: If $m$ is the slope of one of the lines represented by $ax^2+2hxy+by^2=0$, then $(h+bm)^2=$
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: Pair of Straight Lines
questions.explanation: Dividing by $x^2$, $bm^2+2hm+a=0$, so $bm=-h\pm\sqrt{h^2-ab}$, giving $(h+bm)^2=h^2-ab$.

questions.q: $\cot12^\circ\cot102^\circ+\cot102^\circ\cot66^\circ+\cot66^\circ\cot12^\circ=$
questions.explanation: Since $12^\circ+102^\circ+66^\circ=180^\circ$, the identity $\cot A\cot B+\cot B\cot C+\cot C\cot A=1$ (for $A+B+C=180^\circ$) gives the value $1$.

questions.q: $(\sin\theta+\cos\theta)(\tan\theta+\cot\theta)=$
questions.explanation: $\tan\theta+\cot\theta=\dfrac{1}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}$, so the product is $\dfrac{\sin\theta+\cos\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}=\sec\theta+\text{cosec}\,\theta$.

questions.q: The sides of a triangle are $6+\sqrt{12}$, $\sqrt{48}$ and $\sqrt{24}$. The tangent of the smallest angle of the triangle is
questions.explanation: The smallest side is $\sqrt{24}=2\sqrt6$; using the cosine rule for the angle opposite it gives $\cos C=\sqrt3/2$, so $C=30^\circ$ and $\tan C=1/\sqrt3$.

questions.q: A simple graph contains 24 edges. Degree of each vertex is 3. The number of vertices is
questions.explanation: Sum of degrees $=2\times\text{edges}=48$; with each vertex of degree 3, the number of vertices is $48/3=16$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\left\{n\sin\dfrac{2\pi}{3n}\cdot\cos\dfrac{2\pi}{3n}\right\}=$
questions.explanation: As $n\to\infty$, $n\sin(2\pi/3n)\to 2\pi/3$ and $\cos(2\pi/3n)\to1$, so the limit is $2\pi/3$.

questions.q: The function $f(x)=[x]$, where $[x]$ denotes the greatest integer not greater than $x$, is
options: continuous for all real values of $x$.
continuous only at rational values of $x$.
continuous for all nonintegral values of $x$.
continuous only at positive integral values of $x$.
questions.explanation: The greatest integer function has jump discontinuities exactly at integers, so it is continuous everywhere else, i.e. at all nonintegral values of $x$.

questions.q: If $a>b>0$, $\sec^{-1}\left(\dfrac{a+b}{a-b}\right)=2\sin^{-1}x$, then $x=$
questions.explanation: With $\theta=\sin^{-1}x$, $\cos2\theta=1-2x^2=\dfrac{a-b}{a+b}$, giving $x^2=\dfrac{b}{a+b}$; since $2\theta\in[0,\pi/2)$, $x$ is positive, so $x=\sqrt{b/(a+b)}$.

questions.q: If $x\ne n\pi$, $x\ne(2n+1)\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, $n\in Z$, then $\dfrac{\sin^{-1}(\cos x)+\cos^{-1}(\sin x)}{\tan^{-1}(\cot x)+\cot^{-1}(\tan x)}=$
questions.explanation: For $x\in(0,\pi/2)$ each term equals $\pi/2-x$, so the ratio simplifies to $(\pi-2x)/(\pi-2x)=1$, which is not among the listed options; KEA awarded a grace mark to everyone for this question (as per KEA key), so no option is truly correct.

questions.q: The general solution of $1+\sin^2x=3\sin x\cdot\cos x$, $\tan x\ne\dfrac{1}{2}$ is
questions.explanation: Dividing by $\cos^2x$ gives $2\tan^2x-3\tan x+1=0$, i.e. $\tan x=1/2$ or $1$; excluding $1/2$, $\tan x=1$ gives $x=n\pi+\pi/4$.

questions.q: The least positive integer $n$, for which $\dfrac{(1+i)^n}{(1-i)^{n-2}}$ is positive, is
questions.explanation: Since $(1-i)^2=-2i$ and $(1+i)/(1-i)=i$, the expression equals $-2i^{n+1}$; at $n=1$ this is $-2i^2=2$, a positive real number, so the least such $n$ is $1$.

questions.q: If $x+iy=(-1+i\sqrt3)^{2010}$, then $x=$
questions.explanation: $-1+i\sqrt3=2\,\text{cis}(120^\circ)$, so raising to the $2010$th power gives $2^{2010}\text{cis}(2010\times120^\circ)=2^{2010}\text{cis}(0^\circ)=2^{2010}$, purely real.

questions.q: The greatest value of $x$ satisfying $21\equiv385\ (\text{mod}\ x)$ and $587\equiv167\ (\text{mod}\ x)$ is
questions.explanation: $x$ must divide $385-21=364=2^2\cdot7\cdot13$ and $587-167=420=2^2\cdot3\cdot5\cdot7$; their GCD is $28$.

questions.q: The number $(49^2-4)(49^3-49)$ is divisible by
questions.explanation: $49^2-4=47\times51$ and $49^3-49=49\times48\times50$, so the product is $47\times51\times49\times48\times50=281887200$, which is exactly divisible by $6!=720$, $5!=120$ and $7!=5040$, but not by $9!$.

questions.q: The least positive integer $x$ satisfying $2^{2010}\equiv3x\ (\text{mod}\ 5)$ is
questions.explanation: Powers of $2$ mod $5$ cycle with period $4$; since $2010\equiv2\pmod4$, $2^{2010}\equiv2^2\equiv4\pmod5$. Then $3x\equiv4\pmod5$ gives $x=3$.

questions.q: If $A$ and $B$ are two square matrices of the same order such that $AB=B$ and $BA=A$, then $A^2+B^2$ is always equal to
questions.explanation: Since $A=BA$, $A^2=A\cdot A=(AB)A=B(A A)$... more directly $A^2=A(BA)=(AB)A=BA=A$, and similarly $B^2=B(AB)=(BA)B=AB=B$, so $A^2+B^2=A+B$.

questions.q: If $A$ is a $3\times3$ nonsingular matrix and if $|A|=3$, then $|(2A)^{-1}|=$
If $A=\begin{bmatrix}3 & 2\\ 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}$, then $A^2+xA+yI=0$ for $(x, y)=$
questions.explanation: By the Cayley-Hamilton theorem, $A$ satisfies $\lambda^2-(\text{trace})\lambda+|A|=0$, i.e. $A^2-4A+I=0$, so $(x,y)=(-4,1)$.

questions.q: The constant term of the polynomial $\begin{vmatrix}x+3 & x & x+2\\ x & x+1 & x-1\\ x+2 & 2x & 3x+1\end{vmatrix}$ is
questions.explanation: The constant term is the determinant's value at $x=0$: $\begin{vmatrix}3&0&2\\0&1&-1\\2&0&1\end{vmatrix}=3(1)-0+2(-2)=-1$.

questions.q: If $\vec a$, $\vec b$ and $\vec c$ are nonzero coplanar vectors, then $\left[2\vec a-\vec b\ \ 3\vec b-\vec c\ \ 4\vec c-\vec a\right]=$
questions.explanation: Since $\vec a,\vec b,\vec c$ are coplanar, every linear combination of them also lies in that plane, so the scalar triple product of any three such combinations is always $0$.

questions.q: A space vector makes the angles $150^\circ$ and $60^\circ$ with the positive direction of X- and Y-axes. The angle made by the vector with the positive direction of Z-axis is
questions.explanation: Using $\cos^2150^\circ+\cos^260^\circ+\cos^2\gamma=1$: $3/4+1/4+\cos^2\gamma=1$, so $\cos\gamma=0$, i.e. $\gamma=90^\circ$.

questions.q: If $\vec a$, $\vec b$ and $\vec c$ are unit vectors, such that $\vec a+\vec b+\vec c=\vec 0$, then $3\vec a\cdot\vec b+2\vec b\cdot\vec c+\vec c\cdot\vec a=$
questions.explanation: By symmetry the three unit vectors are mutually at $120^\circ$, so each dot product equals $-1/2$; then $3(-1/2)+2(-1/2)+(-1/2)=-3$.

questions.q: If $i, j, k$ are unit vectors along the positive direction of X-, Y- and Z-axes, then a FALSE statement in the following is
questions.explanation: The cyclic sum $i\cdot(j\times k)+j\cdot(k\times i)+k\cdot(i\times j)=1+1+1=3\ne0$, so statement 1 is false; the other three cyclic sums correctly evaluate to $0$.

questions.q: In $P(X)$, the power set of a nonempty set $X$, a binary operation $*$ is defined by $A*B=A\cup B\ \forall\ A, B\in P(X)$. Under $*$, a TRUE statement is
questions.explanation: Union is commutative and associative, and $\emptyset$ acts as the identity; but no set other than $\emptyset$ has an inverse under union, so the inverse law fails.

questions.q: The inverse of 2010 in the group $Q^+$ of all positive rationals under the binary operation $*$ defined by $a*b=\dfrac{ab}{2010}$, $\forall\ a, b\in Q^+$, is
questions.explanation: The identity element $e$ satisfies $ae/2010=a$, so $e=2010$; since $2010$ is itself the identity, it is its own inverse.

questions.q: If the three functions $f(x)$, $g(x)$ and $h(x)$ are such that $h(x)=f(x)\cdot g(x)$ and $f'(x)\cdot g'(x)=c$, where $c$ is a constant, then $\dfrac{f''(x)}{f(x)}+\dfrac{g''(x)}{g(x)}+\dfrac{2c}{f(x)\cdot g(x)}$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $h''=f''g+2f'g'+fg''=f''g+fg''+2c$; dividing by $h=fg$ gives exactly the given expression, so it equals $h''(x)/h(x)$.

questions.q: The derivative of $e^{ax}\cos bx$ with respect to $x$ is $re^{ax}\cos\left(bx+\tan^{-1}\dfrac{b}{a}\right)$. When $a>0, b>0$, the value of $r$ is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{d}{dx}(e^{ax}\cos bx)=e^{ax}(a\cos bx-b\sin bx)$, which can be written as $\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\,e^{ax}\cos(bx+\tan^{-1}(b/a))$, so $r=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$.

questions.q: If $x=a\cos^3\theta$ and $y=a\sin^3\theta$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=$
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{3a\sin^2\theta\cos\theta}{-3a\cos^2\theta\sin\theta}=-\tan\theta=-\sqrt[3]{y/x}$, using $\sin\theta=(y/a)^{1/3}$, $\cos\theta=(x/a)^{1/3}$.

questions.q: If $y=\tan^{-1}\sqrt{x^2-1}$, then the ratio $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}:\dfrac{dy}{dx}=$
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{x^2-1}}$ and $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=-\dfrac{2x^2-1}{x^2(x^2-1)^{3/2}}$; their ratio simplifies to $\dfrac{1-2x^2}{x(x^2-1)}$.

questions.q: $P$ is the point of contact of the tangent from the origin to the curve $y=\log_e x$. The length of the perpendicular drawn from the origin to the normal at $P$ is
questions.explanation: The tangent from the origin touches at $P=(e,1)$ (since the tangent line $y-\ln x_0=(x-x_0)/x_0$ passes through the origin only when $x_0=e$); the normal there is $ex+y-(e^2+1)=0$, whose distance from the origin is $\sqrt{e^2+1}$.

questions.q: For the curve $4x^5=5y^4$, the ratio of the cube of the subtangent at a point on the curve to the square of the subnormal at the same point is
questions.explanation: With $y'=x^4/y^3$, the subtangent is $y^4/x^4$ and the subnormal is $x^4/y^2$; using $y^4=(4/5)x^5$, the ratio (subtangent)$^3$/(subnormal)$^2$ simplifies to $(4/5)^4$.

questions.q: The set of real values of $x$ for which $f(x)=\dfrac{x}{\log x}$ is increasing, is
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=\dfrac{\log x-1}{(\log x)^2}\ge0$ requires $\log x\ge1$, i.e. $x\ge e$.

questions.q: A wire of length 20 cm is bent in the form of a sector of a circle. The maximum area that can be enclosed by the wire is
questions.explanation: With perimeter $2r+r\theta=20$, area $A=10r-r^2$; maximizing gives $r=5$ and $A=25$ sq. cm.

questions.q: Two circles centered at $(2, 3)$ and $(5, 6)$ intersect each other. If the radii are equal, the equation of the common chord is
questions.explanation: For equal radii, the common chord is the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining the centres; its midpoint is $(3.5,4.5)$ and it has slope $-1$, giving $x+y-8=0$.

questions.q: Equation of the circle centered at $(4, 3)$ touching the circle $x^2+y^2=1$ externally, is
questions.explanation: Distance between centres $=5$; for external tangency the new radius is $5-1=4$, giving $(x-4)^2+(y-3)^2=16$, i.e. $x^2+y^2-8x-6y+9=0$.

questions.q: The points $(1, 0)$, $(0, 1)$, $(0, 0)$ and $(2k, 3k)$, $k\ne0$ are concyclic if $k=$
questions.explanation: The circle through $(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)$ is $x^2+y^2-x-y=0$; substituting $(2k,3k)$ gives $13k^2-5k=0$, so $k=5/13$ (excluding $k=0$).

questions.q: The locus of the point of intersection of the tangents drawn at the ends of a focal chord of the parabola $x^2=-8y$ is
questions.explanation: The locus of intersection of tangents at the ends of a focal chord is the directrix; for $x^2=-8y$ ($4a=8$), the directrix is $y=2$.

questions.q: The condition for the line $y=mx+c$ to be a normal to the parabola $y^2=4ax$ is
questions.explanation: The standard condition for $y=mx+c$ to be a normal to $y^2=4ax$ is $c=-2am-am^3$.

questions.q: The eccentric angle of the point $(2, \sqrt3)$ lying on $\dfrac{x^2}{16}+\dfrac{y^2}{4}=1$ is
questions.explanation: With $x=4\cos\theta$, $y=2\sin\theta$: $\cos\theta=1/2$ and $\sin\theta=\sqrt3/2$, so $\theta=\pi/3$.

questions.q: The distance of the focus of $x^2-y^2=4$, from the directrix which is nearer to it, is
questions.explanation: Here $a=b=2$, $e=\sqrt2$; the focus is at $ae=2\sqrt2$ and the nearer directrix at $a/e=\sqrt2$, so the distance between them is $\sqrt2$.

questions.q: If $\displaystyle\int f(x)\sin x\cdot\cos x\,dx=\dfrac{1}{2(b^2-a^2)}\log f(x)+c$, where $c$ is the constant of integration, then $f(x)=$
questions.explanation: Differentiating both sides gives $f'(x)/f(x)^2=(b^2-a^2)\sin2x$; integrating, $-1/f(x)=-\dfrac{(b^2-a^2)}{2}\cos2x$, so $f(x)=\dfrac{2}{(b^2-a^2)\cos2x}$.

questions.q: If $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{\sqrt x}{x(x+1)}dx=k\tan^{-1}m$, then $(k, m)$ is
questions.explanation: Substituting $x=t^2$ turns the integral into $\int\dfrac{2}{t^2+1}dt=2\tan^{-1}t+C=2\tan^{-1}\sqrt x+C$, so $(k,m)=(2,\sqrt x)$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4}\dfrac{\sin x+\cos x}{3+\sin2x}dx=$
questions.explanation: With $t=\sin x-\cos x$, $3+\sin2x=4-t^2$; the limits become $t=-1$ to $t=0$, giving $\int\dfrac{dt}{4-t^2}=\dfrac{1}{4}\log3$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int_0^1 x(1-x)^{3/2}dx=$
questions.explanation: Using the Beta function, $\displaystyle\int_0^1x(1-x)^{3/2}dx=B(2,5/2)=\dfrac{\Gamma(2)\Gamma(5/2)}{\Gamma(9/2)}=\dfrac{4}{35}$.

questions.q: The area bounded by the curve $y=\begin{cases}x^2, & x<0\\ x, & x\ge0\end{cases}$ and the line $y=4$ is
The order and degree of the differential equation $y=\dfrac{dp}{dx}x+\sqrt{a^2p^2+b^2}$ where $p=\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ (here $a$ and $b$ are arbitrary constants) respectively are
questions.explanation: $dp/dx=d^2y/dx^2$, so the order is 2; isolating and squaring the radical, $(y-xp')^2=a^2p^2+b^2$, makes the highest derivative appear squared, so the degree is also 2.

questions.q: The general solution of the differential equation $2x\dfrac{dy}{dx}-y=3$ is a family of
questions.explanation: Solving the linear equation gives $y=C\sqrt x-3$, i.e. $(y+3)^2=C^2x$, which represents a family of parabolas.
